constitution.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999
constitution.note: The Commission's copy of the 1999 text as enacted, without the alterations of 2010-2023. Ss. 3 and First Schedule (36 states, 768 LGAs, and 6 FCT area councils), 7 (elected local government councils), 8 (referendums on new states and LGAs), 48-49 (Senate and House), 69 and 110 (recall), 71 and 112-115 (constituencies), 76-77, 116-117, 132-134, and 178-179 (elections), 91 (Houses of Assembly), 231 (judges appointed), and Third Schedule Part II, para. 4 (State Independent Electoral Commissions).

classes.name_en: Chairmen of the 768 state local government councils
classes.locator: https://nigeriarights.gov.ng/files/constitution.pdf (s. 7(1): democratically elected local government councils; Third Schedule Part II, para. 4(a): each State Independent Electoral Commission organizes the elections to the local government councils within the State)

classes.disposition_reason: No official source publishes the state commissions' returns together; INEC publishes none, and the commissions' own sites tried did not resolve or answered 403 on 2026-11-17.

classes.locator: https://www.inecnigeria.org/about (FEC: 1960-1966: conducted the 1964 federal and 1965 regional elections)
classes.note: Regional assemblies were elected in the 1950s and 1960s; the military government suspended them in January 1966 and replaced the regions with 12 states in May 1967.
classes.disposition_reason: INEC publishes no returns of the ECN or FEC regional elections, and no official copy of their gazetted results was reachable.

classes.name: National Constitutional Conference delegates election
classes.name_en: Elected delegates to the National Constitutional Conference (1994)
classes.locator: https://www.inecnigeria.org/about (NEC: 1987-1993; NECON: 1995-1998)
classes.note: Delegates were elected by constituency in May 1994 alongside members nominated by the government; the conference sat in 1994-1995. The 1977 and 1988 Constituent Assemblies were chosen indirectly by local government councils.
classes.disposition_reason: No official return of the 1994 delegate elections is published by INEC or reachable elsewhere.

dates.note: Month only: the delegate elections of May 1994. Date as widely recorded; no official notice or return for it was reachable in this session (INEC's site keeps no results archive before 2019).

classes.name: Referendum
classes.name_en: Referendums on the creation of a state or local government area
classes.locator: https://nigeriarights.gov.ng/files/constitution.pdf (s. 8(1)(b) and (3)(b): a request for a new State or LGA must be approved in a referendum by at least two-thirds of the people of the area)
classes.note: Constitutional amendments under s. 9 need the National Assembly and two-thirds of the state Houses, not a popular vote. INEC is charged with any referendum the Constitution requires.
classes.disposition_reason: No referendum has been held under the 1999 Constitution: no new state or LGA has passed the s. 8 procedure, and Nigeria has never held a national referendum.

classes.name: Recall referendum
classes.name_en: Recall of members of the National Assembly, Houses of Assembly, and FCT area councils
classes.locator: https://nigeriarights.gov.ng/files/constitution.pdf (ss. 69 and 110: a petition of more than half of the registered voters of the constituency, then a referendum by INEC within ninety days; Electoral Act 2026, s. 117 for area councillors)
classes.note: INEC has received and verified recall petitions, but none has reached the referendum stage.
classes.disposition_reason: No recall referendum has ever been held; petitions have failed at INEC's signature verification.

classes.name: Party primaries
classes.name_en: Party primaries and consensus nominations
classes.locator: https://www.inecnigeria.org/documents/Electoral-Act-2026.pdf (s. 84: nominations by direct primaries or consensus; s. 86: direct primaries under each party's guidelines; s. 87: consensus candidates)
classes.disposition_reason: Parties run their own primaries; INEC only monitors them and receives the nominees, and publishes no primary returns.

classes.name: Presiding officers
classes.name_en: Senate President, Speakers, and other officers elected by their own houses
classes.locator: https://nigeriarights.gov.ng/files/constitution.pdf (s. 50: the Senate and House elect their presiding officers from among their members; s. 92: the same for each House of Assembly)
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the members of each house, not by voters.

classes.name: Traditional rulers
classes.name_en: Emirs, obas, obis, and other traditional rulers
classes.locator: https://nigeriarights.gov.ng/files/constitution.pdf (no provision elects traditional rulers; their selection is governed by state chieftaincy laws)
classes.disposition_reason: Selected by kingmakers and approved by state governments under state chieftaincy laws, not by public election.

classes.name: Judges
classes.name_en: Judicial offices
classes.locator: https://nigeriarights.gov.ng/files/constitution.pdf (ss. 231, 238, 250, and 271: the President or Governor appoints judges on the recommendation of the National Judicial Council)
classes.disposition_reason: Nigeria elects no judges; all are appointed.

classes.name: Voting abroad
classes.name_en: Diaspora or out-of-country representation
classes.locator: https://www.inecnigeria.org/documents/Electoral-Act-2026.pdf (Part III: registration and voting only in person at a polling unit in Nigeria)
classes.disposition_reason: Nigeria has no out-of-country voting and no seats for citizens abroad or for any non-territorial group.
